clue.text: Weapon over our country coming in low

indicators.note: coming in tells us the following pieces enter the word for low

parts.note: taken as written
over can mean on, as in a matter on or over which people talk
for a British setter, our country is Great Britain, GB

explanation.surface: Some weapon passes overhead as it swoops low over the homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' wants to be a positional link; here it gives ON. 'our country' is GB because the setter is British, and 'coming in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The English archer's tall bow was a famous medieval weapon.

clue.text: Clumsy fellow producing rubble

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of the letters of rubble

explanation.surface: An awkward chap leaves a heap of debris behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is the anagram signal: the letters of RUBBLE are worked into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lubber is a big, awkward, clumsy person, as in landlubber.

clue.text: Roman mare took this cure in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A Roman horse swallowed this remedy while in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Romans called the Mediterranean Mare Nostrum, 'our sea', so the Latin word mare took this word after it; 'mare' pretends to be a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin it means 'ours', following mare in the Roman name for that sea; it is also a quack medicine or pet remedy.

clue.text: Biters sticking out of the bucket in a resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning the letters of the bucket are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Protruding teeth emerge from a seaside bucket at a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is the anagram signal, read as re-sort: THEBUCKET rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Protruding front teeth are colloquially called by this name.

clue.text: Discreet watering-hole recommended

parts.note: a well is a source of water, a place to draw it
advised means recommended

explanation.surface: A tactful pub recommendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watering-hole' suggests a pub, but here it is a WELL, a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wisely and with careful judgment is being prudent, discreet.

clue.text: Family rejected name of movement

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for name is read backwards

parts.note: to name a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: A family disowns the name of some political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' signals the reversal of the verb sense of 'name'. 'of movement' is an adjectival definition; the surface makes movement sound like a political campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic is the adjective for energy or motion, relating to bodies in motion.

clue.text: Principal island in the West Indies

explanation.surface: The main island in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A key point or figure is the main one; a cay or low islet in the Caribbean is also so spelt.

clue.text: Uplifting part of joint composition

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting tongue of a mortise-and-tenon joint

explanation.surface: Part of a shared piece of music is inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' in a down entry turns TENON upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical piece written for nine players or voices.

clue.text: A tree so variegated is a hybrid

indicators.note: variegated means of mixed colours, suggesting the letters of a tree so are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tree with multicoloured leaves is a crossbred variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' fits the gardening picture but is the anagram signal for ATREESO.
explanation.definitionFit: This rose type is a garden cross, bred from China roses and scented like tea.

clue.text: Very thick mane protecting animal

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so the word for mane encloses the animal

parts.note: a crest is the mane or ridge of hair on an animal's neck
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A horse's very dense mane shields some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' signals the container. 'Very thick' means very stupid, not dense hair, and a horse's crest is the ridge of its neck where the mane grows.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of crass, meaning grossly stupid or insensitive.

clue.text: Sort of English marble at the bottom

parts.note: Basic English is a simplified form of English with a vocabulary of 850 words
an ally (or alley) is a large playing marble

explanation.surface: Some kind of English marble lies at the base of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: BASIC English was a reduced vocabulary devised by C. K. Ogden; an ALLY is a children's marble, once made of alabaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Basically means fundamentally, at heart, which is the sense of 'at bottom'.

clue.text: Animal in New York State

parts.note: Ala. is the abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted somewhere in New York State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York State' reads as one place, but it is two pieces: NY and ALA (Alabama).
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a southern African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Soames's Irene showing a lot of regret?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word regret, here losing its first letter

explanation.surface: In Galsworthy's novels, Soames's wife Irene is a source of great regret to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Soames Forsyte married Irene Heron in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, so his Irene was a Heron; the question mark flags the pun on her maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene's maiden name was Heron, and this white wading bird is a kind of heron.

clue.text: Soldiers wash here, but also in mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of but also in are thrown into disorder; it is also the soldiers' dining hall

explanation.surface: Troops clean up in one place, but they also do so in the mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the army canteen, completing the barracks picture, but it is the anagram signal for BUTALSOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In military slang the ablutions are the washrooms of a camp or barracks.

clue.text: Marsh flower found in slackest current

parts.note: loosest means slackest, least taut
rife means widespread or current

explanation.surface: A wetland bloom grows where the stream flows most sluggishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' sounds like a stream in the marsh, but it is the adjective RIFE, meaning prevalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple and yellow forms of this plant grow in damp places by water.

clue.text: Against intervening in a tyrannical state, showing impassivity

indicators.note: intervening in means coming between, so the letter for against goes inside the long word

parts.note: imperiousness is the state of being domineering or tyrannical
v., short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone opposes interfering in a despotic country and shows no emotion about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intervening in' puts V (versus, against) into IMPERIOUSNESS between the R and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unmoved and unaffected by feeling, impassive, is to be unreachable by emotion.

clue.text: You can't be well off on this

definitions.text: You can't be well off on this

parts.words: You can't be well off on this
parts.note: reads like a comment on low pay, but means time off work granted because one is not well

explanation.surface: A complaint that some allowance will never make you rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well off' looks like wealthy; it means off work while well, which is impossible on this kind of absence.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence from work because of illness is only allowed for the unwell.

clue.text: Seamstress initially imitating honeycomb pattern

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of seamstress

parts.note: mocking means imitating, mimicking

explanation.surface: A dressmaker starts copying a honeycomb design.
explanation.walkthrough: The seamstress fits the needlework picture; only her first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This decorative gathered stitching forms a honeycomb-like pattern on fabric.

clue.text: Synthetic cream massaged into side

indicators.note: massaged into suggests the letters of synthetic cream being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Artificial cream is rubbed into someone's flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like part of the body receiving the massage; in sport a side is a team, and this is the football club of Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports side is a team, and this is a well-known English football club.

clue.text: Name a French poet's sisters

parts.note: un is French for a
Thomas Hood was an English poet of the 19th century

explanation.surface: A French poet names his sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas HOOD wrote 'The Song of the Shirt'; the possessive 's links his name to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are sisters, and the body of nuns collectively is called this.

clue.text: Play in which you will find "The wind and the rain"?

definitions.text: Play in which you will find "The wind and the rain"?

parts.words: Play in which you will find "The wind and the rain"?
parts.note: suggests the Shakespeare play holding that song, but it is a storm, full of wind and rain, and also a Shakespeare play's title

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking which Shakespeare play includes the song 'The wind and the rain'.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is from Twelfth Night, the obvious false path; the play wanted is the one named after a storm, which literally contains wind and rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm brings wind and rain, and Shakespeare's late play takes its name from one.

clue.text: Burrowing rodent found in the Ark

explanation.surface: A digging creature was among the animals aboard Noah's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis says Noah built the Ark of gopher wood, so the word is literally in the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American burrowing pocket rodent; and the unknown timber of Noah's vessel in Genesis.

clue.text: Agreement to give French aircraft a tow initially

parts.note: Concord(e) was the Anglo-French supersonic airliner

indicators.note: initially means take just the opening letter of tow

explanation.surface: A deal is struck to let a French plane be towed at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: CONCORD is the airliner without its final E; add A as written and T, the first letter of 'tow', which 'initially' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal treaty, especially one between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Muse changing ends to declaim

indicators.note: ends tells us the other extreme letter of the Muse's name also shifts, the final one moving to the front
changing signals that a letter of the Muse's name shifts position, here the opening one going to the back

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry

explanation.surface: A Muse switches her approach and starts reciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ends' swaps the first and last letters of ERATO, the E going to the back and the O to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak pompously, holding forth as an orator would.

clue.text: Dance where one should try to keep well away from the bar

definitions.text: Dance where one should try to keep well away from the bar

parts.words: Dance where one should try to keep well away from the bar
parts.note: reads like advice to a dancer to avoid the pub, but means a Caribbean dance in which performers bend backwards under a low pole without touching it

explanation.surface: A dance at which the sensible guest avoids the drinks counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bar' sounds like a pub counter; it is the horizontal pole dancers pass beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: This West Indian dance has dancers lean back to pass under a lowering pole.

clue.text: False ideas.I note about work

indicators.note: about means placed around, so I and the note enclose the word for work

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
to do is to work or perform a task

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that their notions about a job are mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. The definition is Latin, Francis Bacon's word for the 'idols' or fallacies that mislead the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon's idola are fallacies or misconceptions that distort human reasoning.

clue.text: Shavian woman takes little one to see the Queen

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the heroine of Shaw's Pygmalion
Beth March is one of the four sisters of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

explanation.surface: A woman from a Shaw play brings her small child to meet the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little one' sounds like a child but means one of the Little Women, BETH March.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth II was the reigning British monarch when this crossword appeared.

clue.text: Destroy plant I've dropped.

indicators.note: dropped means left out, so the letters of I've are removed from the plant

parts.note: endive is a salad plant related to chicory
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone has dropped a plant and ruined it.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDIVE loses IVE, the letters of 'I've'.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to finish it off, kill it or wreck it.

clue.text: Gallery finds finale a welcome surprise

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
a finale is the end of a performance

explanation.surface: A theatre audience high up finds the show's closing scene pleasantly unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British theatre the GODS are the cheapest seats in the top gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of good fortune that arrives just when needed.

clue.text: English reader for a German prince

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially of lessons in church or at a university

explanation.surface: An English lecturer stands in for a German royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electors were the princes of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to choose the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Holy Roman Empire certain princes held the right to vote for the emperor.
